citations.description: _jira_dc_harness_ready fixture only calls wait_for_jira_dc_ready(); no refuse-if-not-fresh mechanism

findings.criterion: `jira-dc-up` brings up a **fresh** instance (`--force-recreate`, and the fixture refuses to run against a container it did not start into a known-clean state), so an interrupted previous teardown cannot leak stale Jira state into the next run
findings.detail: The Makefile's `jira-dc-up` target (line 181) does include `--force-recreate`, satisfying the first half of this criterion. However, the second half — "the fixture refuses to run against a container it did not start into a known-clean state" — is not implemented anywhere in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` or `test_harness_smoke.py`. The `_jira_dc_harness_ready` session fixture only calls `wait_for_jira_dc_ready()`, which polls until the harness answers REST; it does not check whether the container was started fresh by `jira-dc-up` or is a pre-existing container from an interrupted previous run. No mechanism exists in the fixture code to detect or refuse a non-fresh container state.
